name: Côtes du Vivarais

limits: For red wine, Grenache: at least 30%
For red wine, Syrah: at least 40%
For rosé wine, Syrah: at least 10%
For white wine, Grenache Blanc: at least 50%
For white wine, Clairette and Marsanne together: at least 30%
For white wine, Viognier and Roussanne together: at most 10%

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Syrah and Grenache sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

blurb.text: An appellation in the northwestern extreme of the southern Rhône, made in nine communes of the Ardèche and five of the Gard. The Gorges of the Ardèche cut through it. It became an AOC in 1999, with Grenache and Syrah as main allowed grapes.
